summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and a history of recurrent diabetic foot ulcers was admitted for hyperglycemia with blood glucose over 500. The elevated sugars were attributed to a worsening left calcaneal osteomyelitis. She was not in DKA, and her blood sugar responded well to insulin. She underwent hemodialysis for volume overload, which improved her respiratory status and heart failure symptoms. Her sodium, which was initially low, normalized with fluid restriction. Antibiotics were briefly adjusted but reverted to her home regimen of vancomycin and ceftazidime per her preference. She was deemed a high-risk candidate for her upcoming below-the-knee amputation and advised to seek cardiology clearance. She was discharged home with services, continuing her insulin, antibiotics with dialysis, and all other home medications except gabapentin, which was discontinued.
